sources.title: RabbitMQ .NET/C# Client API Guide
sources.finding: RabbitMQ.Client 7 uses the RabbitMQ.Client API including IChannel. Connections are intended to be long-lived and channels are reused according to the client guide; the P1 scope can use the official client without adding a transport abstraction that would become generic infrastructure policy.

sources.title: Consumer Acknowledgements and Publisher Confirms
sources.finding: Publisher confirms establish broker acceptance of a published message; consumer delivery acknowledgements are independent and must be sent only after the consumer's own successful processing. The P1 dispatcher must not mark an outbox record published before confirm.

sources.title: RabbitMQ Reliability Guide
sources.finding: Acknowledgements and confirms produce at-least-once delivery characteristics, so consumer-side duplicate protection remains an inbox/idempotency concern rather than a claim that the P1 transport foundation is exactly-once.

sources.title: RabbitMQ .NET client releases
sources.finding: The official client release record lists stable 7.x releases including v7.2.1. Any exact centrally managed package version remains subject to governed restore, license, and build validation before implementation.

decision: Use the official RabbitMQ.Client 7.x package family for the authority-required post-commit dispatcher. Require publisher confirms before recording dispatch completion; retain the committed outbox as durable source of pending delivery. Keep consumer acknowledgement/inbox and all domain reactions separately governed.
limitations: This evidence authorizes only technical RabbitMQ.Client compatibility and confirmed post-commit transport refinement. It does not authorize a Product event catalog, public event contract, Connected Product broker access, consumer business handler, inbox implementation, durable-work semantics, or arbitrary queue-per-customer topology.
The exact exchange, queue, dead-letter, retry, and quorum configuration remains limited to the bounded P1-006 technical topology and must not encode owner-domain semantics.
Refresh these sources before changing the client major version, broker protocol, durability semantics, or topology beyond the accepted ADR-0001 boundary.
